summary: Sudan requires an embassy visa obtained in advance for nearly every nationality, but the civil war that began in April 2023 has effectively closed the country to tourism — many Sudanese missions abroad have suspended or scaled back visa services, and Western governments advise against all travel.

primarySources.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of the Sudan

defaultSource.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of the Sudan

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required for travelers over 1 year of age arriving from countries with risk of yellow fever transmission; vaccination is also generally recommended for travel to parts of Sudan.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of the Sudan

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not checked at the border, but cover including medical evacuation is essential — most mainstream insurers exclude Sudan because of the war, so specialist cover is usually needed.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of the Sudan

onwardTicket.text: Not formally published as a requirement; with scheduled flights suspended or rerouted by the war, entry is in practice governed by the visa and sponsorship arranged in advance.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of the Sudan

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; consulates may ask about means of support during the application.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of the Sudan

currencyLimits.text: Declare foreign currency on arrival. Import and export of Sudanese pounds is restricted, and official and market exchange rates diverge sharply.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of the Sudan

notes: Alcohol may not be brought into Sudan.
Photographing bridges, airports, military sites and infrastructure can lead to detention — photography permits have historically been required.

payments.text: The banking system has largely broken down during the war — international cards and ATMs do not work for foreign visitors, so US dollars in cash are essential. Exchange rates vary widely between official and market channels.

safety.text: Sudan has been in full-scale civil war between the armed forces and the RSF since April 2023. Governments uniformly advise against all travel: fighting affects Khartoum, Darfur and much of the country, most embassies have evacuated, and consular help is unavailable.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Sudan Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to February is the cooler dry season — in normal times the window for Nile valley trips and the Meroë pyramids, though tourism is suspended by the war.

tips.text: Sudan is in active civil war — governments advise against all travel. Khartoum airport and much of the capital have been battlegrounds, land routes are dangerous, and no meaningful consular assistance is available in-country.
Many Sudanese embassies and consulates have suspended or scaled back visa services since the war began — check whether the mission serving your country is actually operating before planning anything.
Travelers who do enter must register with the authorities within three days of arrival, and separate permits have historically been required to travel outside the capital and to take photographs.
Evidence of travel to Israel in your passport can lead to refusal of a visa or entry.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Sudan?
faq.answer: Yes — nearly every nationality needs a visa obtained in advance from a Sudanese embassy, normally backed by a local sponsor or travel-agency invitation. In practice the civil war has suspended most tourist visa issuance, and many Sudanese missions abroad are not processing applications.

faq.question: Is Sudan open to tourists?
faq.answer: Effectively no. Since fighting broke out in April 2023 the country has been in civil war — tourism has stopped, scheduled flights are minimal, and Western governments advise against all travel.

faq.question: Does Sudan have an eVisa or visa on arrival?
faq.answer: No reliable one. Visas are issued in advance by Sudanese embassies; any on-arrival arrangements that existed before the war cannot be counted on. Confirm directly with a functioning Sudanese mission.

faq.question: Can Israeli citizens visit Sudan?
faq.answer: No — Israeli passport holders are not admitted to Sudan, and evidence of travel to Israel in any passport can also cause refusal.

faq.question: Which Sudanese embassy should I apply through?
faq.answer: Normally the mission accredited to your country of residence — but since the war many have suspended services, so you may need to contact several to find one that is operating. Requirements and fees vary considerably between missions.
